The observed 21% RRR exceeds the predicted 16%, but the early stoppage with low power typically inflates the point estimate, no confidence interval was reported, and the primary composite includes a softer component (hospitalization for unstable angina requiring urgent revascularization). Immunogenicity necessitated dose reductions in many participants, and only a press release is available as of the 2017-03-17 cutoff.", "key_evidence": ["HR 0.79 (21% RRR) for primary composite endpoint — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)", "403 primary events (179 treatment, 224 control) in ~10,564 randomized — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)", "Phase 2 placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction -53.4 mg/dL at trial dose — Results of bococizumab, a monoclonal antibody against proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9, from a randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study in statin-treated subjects with hypercholesterolemia.", "Calculator predicted HR 0.838 with 42.5% power — calculator output", "Trial stopped early for efficacy (p=0.027) with 12-month median follow-up — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)", "Injection site reactions significantly more frequent with bococizumab; dose reductions in many subjects — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17) and Results of bococizumab... dose-ranging study", "No confidence interval reported for primary HR; only press release data available — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)"], "what_would_change_this": "Full peer-reviewed publication with confidence intervals, component-specific hazard ratios, and long-term safety data would clarify the precision and durability of the observed benefit.
